record.title: CS/CS/CS/HB 369 (2025): Provenance of Digital Content (died on the House second reading calendar)
record.issuing_body: Florida House of Representatives (2025 Regular Session; sponsor Rep. McFarland)
record.summary: Bill that would have required developers of publicly available generative AI tools to apply provenance data to content made or modified with their tools, or give users a tool to apply it, and to offer a free provenance reader. Provenance data had to follow widely adopted standards, say whether visual content is synthetic, name the developer and exclude personal identifiers. Social media platforms would have had to retain available provenance data and make it visible to users. Violations were to be unfair or deceptive practices, enforced only by the Attorney General after a 30-day cure period; video game services were exempt.
record.notes: Filed on 4 Feb 2025. Reported favourably as committee substitutes by the Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee (17-0, 19 Mar 2025), the Economic Infrastructure Subcommittee (16-0, 31 Mar 2025) and the Commerce Committee (25-0, 15 Apr 2025); placed on the Special Order Calendar for 23 Apr 2025 and temporarily postponed, then indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration on 3 May 2025, and died on the second reading calendar on 16 Jun 2025. The Senate companion, CS/SB 702, died in Ethics and Elections. Had it passed, it would have created s. 501.9741, F.S., and taken effect on 1 Jul 2026. It took its definition of generative AI from s. 106.145, F.S., Florida's law on AI in political advertising.
